sections.h2: Selling a house fast in Maricopa, AZ
sections.html:
Speed in Maricopa comes from settling one decision early: list with an agent, or take a direct cash offer. After that, clear the HOA paperwork and any permit questions so nothing stalls once a buyer shows up. The city sits in Pinal County, so the recorder, the treasurer and the assessor you deal with are all Pinal County offices, whatever the city's name suggests.

Roughly 78,362 people live here as of July 1, 2025, a jump of 34.8 percent over April 2020. About 83.6 percent of homes are owned by the people living in them, and the median owner-occupied home was valued at $377,200 across 2020 to 2024. Many of those homes belong to planned communities, so the HOA is usually your first call.

Start a folder with:

  • The HOA manager's contact, your assessment amount and any special assessment notice
  • Payoff letters for each loan, plus lien releases
  • Permit and final inspection records for a pool, patio or converted garage
  • Paperwork for a solar or battery lease
  • Your newest Pinal County tax statement

sections.h2: Selling a house in an HOA
sections.html:
Under A.R.S. 33-1806, an association with 50 or more properties works from your notice. Tell it in writing that you accepted an offer and pass along the buyer's contact information. The association then has ten days to deliver its governing documents, budget, recent board minutes, financial statements, assessment amounts, any lien and any open violation on your lot.

The buyer signs an acknowledgment at closing that the covenants are binding, and that unpaid assessments can bring collection and foreclosure. Your cost is capped: no more than $400 for the package, up to $100 extra if the buyer needs it rushed and up to $50 for an update. Deeds with certain exemptions under A.R.S. 11-1134 are excused from the process.

Ask the HOA manager for a balance statement before you list. If a paint, landscaping or parked-vehicle violation is open, cure it now. A buyer who finds it in the package may renegotiate.

sections.h2: Permits, building codes and short-term rentals
sections.html:
Construction applications go to the city's Permit Center at 39700 W Civic Center Plaza, and plans are submitted digitally through the online portal. Counter hours run Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with Fridays closed. To get the permit history for your address, call (520) 316-6920 or write to dsd@maricopa-az.gov.

New codes came in this year. Council adopted the 2024 International Codes, the 2023 National Electrical Code and the A117.1-2017 accessibility standard on January 20, 2026, and they took effect February 20, 2026. Anything you permit from here on is judged under them. The Building Official can be reached at 520-316-6932 for code questions.

An expired or unfinished permit is worth resolving before escrow. Ask the Permit Center what closing it out would involve today. Lenders and inspectors notice open permits, and they are cheaper to fix while you still control the timeline.

For a house that has hosted short-term guests, ask Development Services if your address needs a zoning permit or license. A.R.S. 9-500.39 stops a city from banning short-term rentals outright. A city may still ask for an emergency contact, notice to neighbors and a permit fee limited to actual cost or $250.

Bills over $100 may be paid in two halves or all at once. The Pinal County Treasurer's calendar looks like this.

Payment optionDue dateLate after
First halfOctober 15 p.m. on November 1
Second halfMarch 1May 1
Whole year at onceDecember 31After the due date

Late taxes carry a penalty of 16 percent a year, figured monthly, and a parcel left delinquent may go to the county's online tax lien sale in February. A deadline on a weekend rolls to the next business day.

Arizona does not oblige the county to mail you a bill. Check that the Assessor has your current address by calling 520-866-6361. Your escrow officer will show how that year's tax is divided between you and the buyer at closing.

If you owe back taxes, say so up front. Escrow pays them from your proceeds at closing, which is one reason to collect your tax statement early.

sections.h2: Recording the deed with Pinal County
sections.html: A Maricopa deed is recorded by the Pinal County Recorder, which charges $30 per document. That fee also covers the affidavit of property value. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires the affidavit unless the deed carries an exemption notation. Title or escrow staff file everything on the closing date, so you will not have to visit the recorder yourself.

Three items from your folder tend to cause the last-minute delays. A solar or battery lease has to be explained to the buyer, so keep the lease papers where you can find them. Every loan needs a payoff statement, and any recorded lien needs a release. If the HOA package shows a lien on your lot, you will want to know before the buyer does.

None of this is hard on its own. The trouble comes from discovering it in the middle of escrow, when every day counts. An hour spent now with your loan servicer, the HOA manager and the solar company can save a week later.

sections.h2: The steps from offer to closing
sections.html:
The outline is the same for a listing and for a cash sale.

  1. Assemble the HOA, lien, permit, solar and tax papers from the folder above.
  2. Phone the HOA manager for a balance statement and ask about open violations.
  3. Phone the Permit Center about any open permit.
  4. When you accept an offer, send the association its written notice that same day, because its ten-day clock runs from that notice.
  5. Open escrow. Staff there order payoff figures, divide the year's tax between you and the buyer and draft the deed and the affidavit.
  6. On closing day the deed is recorded in Pinal County and you receive proceeds once payoffs and fees are paid.

A cash purchase skips the buyer's loan approval and the lender's appraisal. It does not skip the HOA package or the recording, so begin those first. With a cash buyer, the main timing question becomes how fast the association answers, since its ten days are the longest wait you do not control.

When you call any of these offices, have your parcel number and street address ready. Staff can pull records much faster with the parcel number than with a name.

faqs.q: Is Maricopa, AZ in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: No. The city of Maricopa is in Pinal County. Recording goes through the Pinal County Recorder, property tax goes through the Pinal County Treasurer, and the Pinal County Assessor handles ownership and address changes.

faqs.q: When are Pinal County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due October 1 and late after 5 p.m. on November 1. The second half is due March 1 and late after May 1. A full-year payment is due by December 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Maricopa house that has an open permit?
faqs.a: Yes, but the buyer may ask you to close it first. Call the Permit Center at (520) 316-6920 for the permit history at your address. New building codes took effect February 20, 2026.

faqs.q: How much will my HOA charge when I sell?
faqs.a: State law caps the resale package and lien statement at $400 for the seller, with up to $100 more for a rush within 72 hours and up to $50 for an update. The fees are collected at or after the close of escrow and charged once per transaction.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Pinal County?
faqs.a: The county charges $30 for any document that is recorded. That includes the affidavit of property value and $1 of postage for mailing the document back. Your escrow company normally pays it at closing.
